note: Switch "battleScenes" and the scene frame (test 5, docs/council/2026-11-27-big-scenes.md, thread 46). Every battle is shown as a scene: the ground, the plan, one turning point picked from the state of the game (never by chance), the roll, and a choice after the battle. The turning points and the after-battle choices come from Diodorus (docs/research/big-scenes-history.md); the result names follow Total War's post-battle grades; every number is invention.

turns.when: your plan is a combined attack
turns.text: Your second column is not yet in sight.
turns.why: as at Gela in 405, the parts of the army could not keep time

options.label: Wait for it
options.note: No combined attack: you lose its +2, but nothing can come late.

options.label: Attack with what you have
options.note: Keep the +2; each part may still come too late (1 or 2 on a die costs 2).

turns.text: There is wavering on your wing, among {part}.
turns.source: Diodorus 15.17.2 (Cronium: one wing routs when the other is crushed)

options.label: Send the reserve to them
options.note: They hold, but your reserve is spent: no retreat to camp if you lose.

options.label: Leave them to it
options.note: They hold on 4 or more (3 in 6); if not, -2 and they break first.

turns.text: {general} wants to charge before the line is formed.
turns.why: Leptines at Catana fought "in no cowardly fashion, but without prudence"

options.label: Rein him in
options.note: -1, but a defeat by 1 is only a draw.

options.label: Let him go
options.note: +1, but a defeat becomes a rout (half the army lost).

turns.when: you lead the army in person
turns.text: Your men look for you along the line.
turns.why: a general in the front rank fights for his men's eyes
turns.source: Diodorus 14.53.1 (Dionysius in the fighting at Motya), invention for the odds

options.label: Fight in the front rank
options.note: +1. On a 1 (1 in 6) you are wounded and lose an action next season; wounded in a lost battle, you are killed (1 in 36).

turns.text: The two lines stand a bowshot apart, and neither moves.
turns.why: armies often stood for days before one side moved
turns.source: Diodorus 14.96.2 (the waiting at the Chrysas), invention

options.label: Take the higher ground first
options.note: +1, but even if you win you lose a sixth more men.

win.label: Pursue hard
win.note: They lose a sixth more (a third with horse on open ground). If they kept a reserve, your pursuers are caught in disorder and you lose a sixth instead.

win.label: Sack their camp
win.note: +2 silver and the guard's love, but most of them get away (a quarter lost, not a third).

win.label: Stop the killing and offer terms
win.note: A quarter lost, not a third. Carthage's war weariness +1, and the Greek towns near the field warm to you.

win.label: Take Carthage's secret silver
win.note: Its general offers silver to let its citizens sail home by night. +3 silver, its army breaks up, but your allies may see the ships slip away.

lose.label: Fall back fighting
lose.note: A third of the army is lost, and a beaten army may scatter.

lose.label: Ask a truce to bury the dead, and slip away by night
lose.note: Only a sixth lost and the army holds together, but asking for your dead admits the defeat: the citizens sour and it counts for Carthage.
